note: Parabilis Medicines (formerly FogPharma), Cambridge MA, helicon peptide cancer drugs; listed on Nasdaq (PBLS) in June 2026. Market cap $4.02B as of 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), fresher than the General Catalyst row's $3.85B of 2026-09-25; same band. Entry: GV joined as a new investor in the $66M Series B led by 6 Dimensions Capital (FogPharma's release, 2018-05-16), with Krishna Yeshwant joining the board. The Form D band had dated the entry to the December 2020 Series C filing, a later round; the stage (Growth) is unchanged, the entry date and source are corrected. The S-1 shows GV 2017, L.P. in the Series E and GV 2019, L.P. in the Series F.

Prime Medicine, Cambridge MA, prime editing (Broad Institute, David Liu). Its S-1 (2022-09-23) lists GV 2019, L.P. buying 33,333,331 Series A preferred shares ($33.3M) in the Series A sold in closings of September 2019, November 2020 and April 2021, and GV 2021, L.P. buying $24.0M of the $200M Series B; the company had no round before the Series A (inception September 2019). Entry date is the Series A's first closing. Market cap $511.47M on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), below $1B like the float on file.

PatientPing, Boston, care-coordination notifications. Acquired by Appriss Health in 2021 (the firm's exit line; press reported about $500M). Form D addresses (2015, 2016) are in Boston. The Form D band's Series A entry (2015, Krishna Yeshwant as director) stands; a16z and Leerink led the $31.6M Series B in December 2016.

Pelage Pharmaceuticals, Los Angeles (Form D address, Westwood), regenerative treatment for hair loss. GV led the $16.75M Series A (February 2024) and the $14M Series A-1 (August 2024); a $120M Series B followed in October 2025 with no valuation disclosed, so the row reads below $1B. The Form D band's Series A entry agrees.

Push Security, London, identity and SaaS security. The firm's own post (2023-04-03) says GV led the $15M Series A, which agrees with the Form D band; Redpoint led a $30M Series B in April 2025. No valuation disclosed; below $1B.

Quartet Health, New York, behavioral health care coordination. NeuroFlow acquired Quartet in January 2025 after Quartet divested its telehealth assets (the firm's exit line 'Acquired by NueroFlow, 2025'; Behavioral Health Business, 2025-01-30). Form D addresses are in New York.

Q.ai, Israeli audio and silent-speech AI company (founders Aviad Maizels, Yonatan Wexler, Avi Barliya) that worked in stealth. The firm's own post (2026-01-29): GV co-led Q's inception seed in 2022 with Aleph and followed on in the Series A in 2023; Globes adds that Kleiner Perkins and Spark co-led that Series A and places its early demos in Tel Aviv. Apple acquired Q.ai in January 2026 (TechCrunch, 2026-01-29; reported near $2B).

Plaid, San Francisco, bank-data APIs. Google Ventures was in the $2.8M seed of late 2013 with Spark Capital and NEA (Wikipedia); NEA put in $12.5M in 2014 and Plaid announced a $250M Series C on 2018-12-11, a named later round. Valuation: the unicorn-list $13.4B is the April 2021 Series D; the April 2025 round priced Plaid at $6.1B and a February 2026 employee share sale at $8B (Wikipedia). Aligned to $8B (2026-02) as the Coatue, Ribbit and Spark rows carry; band 1b_plus.

Periscope, San Francisco live-video app (founded February 2014 as Bounty). Its only round was $1.5M in April 2014 from Founder Collective, Maveron, Google Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Bessemer and others (Wikipedia); Menlo's own page labels that round Seed. Twitter bought it in January 2015 before launch and shut the app in March 2021. The Wikidata GR country was a one-word-name join; the company was American. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Pindrop, Atlanta, voice fraud detection and authentication. Wikipedia: Google Capital led the $75M Series C in 2016 with Andreessen Horowitz, GV and others (both Google units in one round); GV was not named in the 2013 Series A (a16z, Citi Ventures) or the February 2015 Series B (IVP). The firm's /ai list shows GV re-investing in November 2018 (the $90M round). No priced round at $1B or more on record; below $1B as the a16z, Felicis and IVP rows carry.

Peerspace, San Francisco marketplace for renting venues and meeting spaces. GV led the $16M Series B (VentureBeat, 2018-07-18) with Foundation Capital and Red Bridge Partners; Peerspace had raised about $19M before, and the firm's listing first carries it in 2018. Still operating (new venue product, September 2026); no valuation disclosed.

Pangea, Silicon Valley security APIs and AI guardrails, founded 2021. BankInfoSecurity (2025-09-18): it raised $51M in all, most recently a $26M Series B in November 2022 led by GV; the firm's /ai list dates GV's first investment to August 2022, the entry date. CrowdStrike agreed to buy Pangea for about $260M in September 2025; the firm's exit line reads 'Acquired by CrowdStrike, 2026'.

Panorama Education, Boston (founded in Cambridge MA), survey and analytics software for schools. Boston.com (2013-10-21): $4M seed co-led by Startup:Education and SoftTech VC with Google Ventures, A-Grade Investments and Yale. General Atlantic led a $60M Series C on 2021-09-02, a named later round. No priced round at $1B or more; below $1B as the a16z, General Catalyst and Spark rows carry.

Parsable, San Francisco connected-worker software for factories. CAI Software (an STG company) acquired it on 2024-09-25 (newswire.com release). GV's entry round is not on record: the $40M Series C of May 2018 (Future Fund lead, with B37, Lightspeed, Airbus Ventures, Aramco Ventures; TechCrunch) names no GV, and the firm's listing first carries Parsable in 2019.

Podium, Lehi UT, messaging, reviews and payments software for local businesses. Summit Partners' release (2017-05-11): $32M Series A led by Accel with Summit Partners, GV and previous investor Y Combinator, so GV entered at the Series A; IVP's post on its $60M Series B (2018-06-07) names GV among the existing investors. Valuation: the unicorn-list $1.5B is the 2020 mark; the $201M Series D of November 2021 priced Podium at $3B (PYMNTS), as the Accel, IVP and Y Combinator rows carry; no priced round since, so stale.

PostHog, open-source product analytics for engineers. The company's own history page: $3.025M seed (April 2020, YC Continuity and 1984 Ventures), then a $9M Series A in December 2020 led by GV (the firm's post of 2020-12-17 says the same), a $15M Series B led by YC (June 2021), a $70M Series D led by Stripe at about $920M with GV participating (June 2025) and a $75M Series E led by Peak XV at about $1.4B (announced 2025-09-30). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on valuation and raises): no later priced round; $1.4B as the Y Combinator row carries.

Pecan AI, Israeli predictive-analytics software. Calcalist (2022-02-02): $66M Series C led by Insight Partners with GV as a new investor, after a $35M Series B led by GGV in May 2021; the firm's /ai list dates GV's investment to November 2021 (the entry date). City aligned with the Insight Partners row. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on raises and valuation): no round after the Series C, layoffs in 2023 and 2024; no priced mark at or above $1B.

Pixie Labs, San Francisco, Kubernetes observability. TechCrunch and the company's release (2020-10-01): $9.15M Series A led by Benchmark with participation from GV, announced as it left stealth; neither names an earlier round. The firm's /ai list dates GV's only investment to October 2018, so the Series A most likely closed in stealth then (entry date from the firm, D7); confidence medium because a 2018 seed cannot be ruled out from these pages. New Relic acquired Pixie in December 2020.

Physna, Cincinnati, geometric deep-learning search for 3D models. Drive Capital led the 2019 Series A and Sequoia the $20M Series B of January 2021 (the release names no GV); Develop3D (2021-07-02): a $56M round led by Tiger Global with GV and Sequoia, taking the total to $86M, so GV entered after the Series B. Shapeways took control of Thangs, the 3D community Physna's search powers, in December 2024; Physna continues with its B2B and government products (Develop3D). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News): no round after July 2021; no priced mark at or above $1B.

Phoebe, London, AI agents that find and fix software failures. $17M seed led by GV and Cherry Ventures (StartupHub.ai and tech.eu, 2025-08-20); the firm's /ai list dates GV's investment to August 2025. Censored: the seed is under 24 months old. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News): no round after the seed; no priced mark at or above $1B.

Polar Signals, Berlin, continuous profiling for cloud software. TechCrunch (2024-03-12): the seed opened in 2021 with $4M from GV and Lightspeed, and a further $6.8M came in 2024 from GV, Spark and Lightspeed ($10.8M in all); the company is incorporated in the US but run from Berlin, where its founder and CEO is based. Dash0 acquired it in August 2026 (Business Insider: 'Dash0 Acquires Berlin Tech Company'; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Dash0, 2026'); fresher than the Spark and Lightspeed rows, which still read private. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Ramp, New York, corporate cards and finance automation. Ramp's release (2025-07-30): $500M at a $22.5B valuation led by ICONIQ, with GV among the new investors (Latham names the round Series E-2); the firm's /ai list dates GV's first investment to July 2025. Valuation: the unicorn-list $32B is November 2025; in June 2026 Ramp raised $750M at $44B (Wikipedia), as most sibling rows carry. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the valuation): September 2026 reports of talks at $60B are not a priced round, so $44B stands.

Quadratic, Boulder CO, a spreadsheet with Python, SQL and AI for data work. TechCrunch and the company's own post (2024-04-02): $5.6M seed led by GV with Catapult Ventures, Betaworks and The Fund Rockies; the firm's /ai list dates GV's investment to August 2023 (the entry date). Check 2026-09-28 (Google News and one web search): no later round reported; no priced mark at or above $1B. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Prudentia Sciences, AI diligence software for life-sciences dealmaking. Wilson Sonsini (2025-01-09): Google Ventures led the $7M financing with Iaso Ventures and Virtue as the company left stealth; Pulse 2.0 calls it the 2024 seed. The firm's /ai list dates GV's investment to October 2024. McKesson Ventures led the $20M Series A with GV following (Pulse 2.0, 2026-01-08), a named later round. No source read places the company in a city.

Pretzel Therapeutics, Waltham MA (research site in Gothenburg), mitochondrial medicines. BioPharma Dive (2022-09-12): launched with a $72.5M Series A, ARCH and Mubadala Capital putting in $15M each, with GV, Invus and Angelini Ventures in the round. No later priced round seen; below $1B.

funding_rounds.lead: ARCH Venture Partners and Mubadala Capital

note: Perceive Bio (perceivebio.com, 6000 Shoreline Drive, South San Francisco), neuroprotective eye therapies. PR Newswire (2025-02-18): Perceive Pharma, spun out of Perceive Biotherapeutics, raised a $15M Series A led by Deerfield with J&J Innovation, Braidwell, GV, the Retinal Degeneration Fund and Catalio. The firm's listing was created nine days later with both GV partners; confidence medium only because the listing's name and site are the parent brand's.

Puppet Labs (later Puppet), Portland OR, infrastructure automation. TechCrunch (2011-11-29): $8.5M Series C led by Cisco, Google Ventures and VMware, all new investors, with existing investors Kleiner Perkins, True Ventures and Radar Partners. Perforce acquired Puppet in April 2022 (Wikipedia).

PlanGrid, San Francisco construction software (YC W12). Fortune (2015-05-13): while still in the accelerator the startup raised 'a small initial funding round of $1.5 million' from Sam Altman, Paul Buchheit, 500 Startups and Google Ventures, the seed TechCrunch reported in May 2012; then $18M led by Sequoia (May 2015, Series A per Wikipedia), a later priced round far above the seed. Tenaya led a $40M round in November 2015. Autodesk bought PlanGrid for $875M in December 2018.

Plexxi, Nashua NH, data-center networking. Its release of 2015-09-14: a $35M round led by an unnamed new investor with Lightspeed, Matrix and North Bridge, bringing the total to $83M; ZDNet's headline of 2016-01-20 reports GV investing in Plexxi. Either way GV came in after the company's earlier rounds (total already $83M), so the entry is a later-stage round: Growth, confidence medium because no page read names GV's round. HPE acquired Plexxi in 2018.

Poynt, Palo Alto, smart payment terminals (founder Osama Bedier, ex-Google Wallet). At launch (2014-10-29) TechCrunch reported a Series A led by Matrix Partners with Webb Investment Network and Nyca, size undisclosed, and the company's own release lists Google Ventures among its backers; neither ties GV to a named round, and no earlier round is reported. Oak HC/FT led the $28M Series B (2015-10-22, no GV named). GoDaddy acquired Poynt (announced December 2020, about $365M).

Product Hunt, San Francisco product-discovery community (YC S14). The firm listed it from September 2014 with Kevin Rose as partner. Its only priced round was the $6.1M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in October 2014 (Wikipedia); the investor lists reported for it do not name Google Ventures, so GV's round is not on record. AngelList acquired Product Hunt in 2016.

Pensando Systems, edge and cloud networking silicon and software. Its release (2019-10-16, datelined San Jose): up to $145M Series C led by HPE and Lightspeed with Goldman Sachs and Equinix, after a $71M Series A and a $62M Series B; GV is not named, and the firm's listing first carries Pensando in 2020, so GV's round (an extension or a later round) is not on record. AMD acquired Pensando in 2022 (about $1.9B). City aligned with the Lightspeed row.

Percolata, Palo Alto, in-store traffic analytics for retailers; on the firm's listing from 2015 (partner Shanna Tellerman). Its Form D of 2017-01-18 (CIK 1696887) reports $9.57M sold of a $14.6M equity offering from Palo Alto, with no GV partner among the directors. No source read gives its fate after 2017 (Google News returns nothing), so status unknown, as the a16z row carries; GV's round is not on record.

Quettra, a Silicon Valley mobile-app analytics and targeting startup of ex-Google, eBay and Microsoft staff; SimilarWeb bought it for about $10M (Globes, 2015-12-10). On the firm's listing from 2014 (partner M.G. Siegler); no source read names its rounds or its city.

Premise Data, San Francisco, crowdsourced market and ground-truth data. The Form D band dated GV's entry to the September 2015 filing (about $50M, Karim Faris a director), but the firm's own listing on googleventures.com already carried Premise in May 2013, so that round was a follow-on and the entry round is not on record: stage undetermined (disputes the band). WestCap led an $85M Series E in January 2021 (release names no GV). No valuation disclosed; below $1B.

PeopleOne Health, employer-sponsored primary-care clinics, Pittsburgh area (Form D address in Oakmont, PA; press calls it Pittsburgh-based). GV and Glen Tullman backed its $32M Series B (MobiHealthNews, 2024-10-25), which agrees with the Form D band's Growth entry. In September 2025 it closed its Pennsylvania clinics to focus on Florida, where it still operates (Boca Raton, December 2025).

Partiful, New York, event invitations app. The firm's own case study gives 'Date Invested: 2021', a year before the company's first named round, the $20M Series A of 2022 led by Andreessen Horowitz (Wikipedia; Business Insider, 2022-11-07); GV therefore entered at the seed stage, but no page read names that round, so the stage is uncited (confidence low). The Series A is the cited later round.

The pre-filled values were one-word-name joins and are removed: Q2 had taken Q2 Holdings' SEC float (public since 2014, $5.8B) and Q1 a German Wikidata country. Paradigm Health, clinical-trials platform that brings research into routine care. Jawlah (2023-01-30): $203M Series A led by ARCH Venture Partners and General Catalyst, which incubated it, with Mubadala Capital, F-Prime Capital, GV and Lux Capital; a $78M Series B followed in December 2025 with the purchase of Flatiron Health's clinical-research business, no valuation disclosed. City: the company's own site gives 175 S. 3rd St, Columbus OH, and the December 2025 press calls it a Columbus startup; fresher than the New York the 2023 coverage and the General Catalyst row carry.

funding_rounds.lead: ARCH Venture Partners and General Catalyst

note: Pager (pager.xyz), a New York consumer app that turns screenshots into shareable, clickable pages; on the firm's list since 2023 with M.G. Siegler. Not the New York health-navigation company Pager (Pager Health) in the Lux Capital book. Homebrew's post title reports a $5.2M seed in November 2022 and search summaries say GV led it, but no page read ties GV to a named round (the Homebrew post now returns 404; WIRED and Medium refuse reading). Status unknown: the company site no longer resolves (checked 2026-09-28, the domain keeps only mail records) and no news since 2022, though the firm still lists it.

Parse, San Francisco mobile backend-as-a-service (YC S11); Facebook bought it in April 2013 (the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Facebook, 2013') and shut the service in January 2017. TechCrunch (2011-11-09): $1.5M earlier from Y Combinator and angels, then a $5.5M Series A led by Ignition Partners; neither names Google Ventures, which listed Parse by May 2013, so GV's round is not on record.

PayRange, Portland OR, mobile payments for vending machines and laundromats; on the firm's list from September 2014 (Kevin Rose). Rounds on record: $2.7M in August 2014, $12M in June 2015 (GeekWire headlines) and $70M in 2020; the articles could not be read, so GV's round is not established. Private-equity firm Ridgeview Partners bought PayRange in September 2024 (Bloomberg headline; the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Ridgeview Partners, 2024').

Periscope Data, San Francisco SQL analytics and visualization. Sisense acquired it in May 2019 (Globes: about $100M; the founder later put it at $130M). On the firm's list from 2016; no source read names its rounds or GV's round.

Pocket (Read It Later until 2012), San Francisco save-for-later app. TechCrunch (2011-07-26): a $2.5M round, the company's first external funding, led by Foundation Capital with Baseline Ventures, Google Ventures and Founder Collective; the article gives it no round name, so the stage is undetermined though the round is known. A $5M round followed in 2012 (Wikipedia). Mozilla acquired Pocket in February 2017 and shut the service on 2025-07-08. Not the Pocket rows in the Accel and Y Combinator books, which are other companies.
